extracted.intended_audience: potential donors and grassroots climate activists seeking funding
extracted.subtask_description: Describes an individual funder's mission, priorities, and selection emphasis for making grants to grassroots climate groups that use nonviolent disruptive tactics; useful for applicants and donors to understand what the fund supports. Focuses on early-stage, ambitious groups judged likely to have outsized impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of nonviolent disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes grants to grassroots climate groups who utilize nonviolent disruption as part of their campaigning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund explicitly supports nonviolent, disruptive, people-powered climate movement tactics because it believes such tactics are necessary to create the social and political will for rapid decarbonization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for grassroots groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are made to grassroots climate groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEF positions itself as a bridge between philanthropy and grassroots activists, staffed by long-time organizers and activists with international networks; it emphasizes funding the courageous work of frontline/grassroots organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on ambitious, early-stage groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds ambitious groups in their early stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because movements are critically underfunded, CEF aims to fill the gap by supporting promising groups early—i.e., those that are ambitious but still nascent and need initial philanthropic backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize groups likely to have outsized impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully vetting the groups most likely to have outsized impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEF evaluates potential grantees for their likelihood of producing outsized impact; as evidence of desirable outcomes, the page cites that since 2022 grantees have mobilized 440,000 people and generated over 230,000 news stories—implying scale of mobilization and media influence are valued impact signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous vetting and expert oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses an extensive network of movement experts and a board of experts in science, activism, and communications to support and vet grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board and team provide expertise, networks, and due diligence capacity; this operational principle implies applicants are assessed by experienced practitioners and that credibility/fit with movement strategy matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational/operational status
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate Emergency Fund is a funding intermediary and venture philanthropy; it is a 501(c)(3) organization (EIN 84-2151545).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEF acts as a 'safe bridge' between funders and activists, indicating its role and legal/tax status are part of how it positions itself to donors and grantees (e.g., tax-deductible donations, intermediary grantmaking).
